ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum achievable legal-reasoning correctness under H1-H8 is: provable soundness AND completeness of every emitted legal conclusion with respect to IDEAL / SCEPTICAL-PREFERRED CERTIFIED ACCEPTANCE over an explicitly committed, finite, defeasible rulebase — the strongest per-query-unique, deterministic, decidable, certificate-carrying acceptance relation available — where (a) every conclusion carries a machine-checkable certificate re-verifiable offline (H5/H8): for grounded-rung conclusions a finite well-founded derivation tree, for ideal/sceptical-preferred conclusions a certified exhaustive-extension certificate (the complete preferred-extension set, or a refutation-complete search trace) checkable offline with zero producer trust; (b) defeater sensitivity is total over the committed rulebase (every admitted defeater that attacks a derivation is guaranteed to defeat or be defeated in the labelling, including cyclic attack structures); (c) every question whose answer depends on unformalized or interpretively contested source text returns typed UNKNOWN (H2). The grounded (well-founded) extension is the maximal TRACTABLE-UNIQUE rung — the unique semantics that is simultaneously per-query-unique, deterministic, polynomial-time, and certificate-carrying — and grounded acceptance is a STRICT SUBSET of ideal acceptance (recorded gap: even attack cycles occurring in real norm-conflict structures, which ideal semantics may decide and grounded leaves undefined). Restricting operation to the grounded rung is a RESOURCE (cost-class) choice governed by an AX-17 certified cost budget — never a possibility bound. No feasible system can additionally guarantee correctness of the natural-language-to-rule formalization step itself, nor resolve genuinely contested interpretation.
ceilings.derivation: (1) Computability, stated honestly. Full first-order defeasible logic is undecidable. CREDULOUS acceptance under preferred/stable semantics is non-unique per query, so credulous SELECTION without a committed tie-break breaks H5 — but that argument does not generalize: sceptical acceptance under preferred semantics, and the ideal and eager semantics (Dung-Mancarella-Toni), are (i) per-query UNIQUE and deterministic (H5 replay holds — computing the full extension set or the unique ideal extension is a total pure function of the frozen rulebase), (ii) decidable on the finite committed rulebase (H3 fail-closed termination holds), (iii) certificate-carrying with finite offline-checkable certificates. What they cost is only the complexity class (co-NP-hard verification vs P-time), and polynomial time is not an H1-H8 invariant anywhere in the freeze — cost is exactly what AX-17 certified budgets govern. The v1 lemma 'grounded is the unique maximal semantics' is therefore corrected: grounded is the unique maximum AMONG TRACTABLE unique-status semantics; ideal/sceptical-preferred certified acceptance is the strictly stronger H1-H8-conforming ceiling, strictly containing grounded acceptance. Per the supreme law the stronger conception IS the ceiling; grounded is its tractable rung, retained by declared cost budget only. (2) Information theory: the bytes of a statute underdetermine legal meaning (open texture; contested interpretation is not a computable function of committed text), so correctness about 'the law itself' is not machine-decidable by ANY system; the supremum is correctness relative to a committed formal rulebase plus honest UNKNOWN at the formalization boundary. (3) H1 closes the only escape hatch: a statistical model cannot be trusted to certify the NL-to-formal mapping, so that mapping enters only as attested, admitted input whose certificate records who/what asserted it. Exceeding this restated ceiling requires deciding an undecidable question or a question not encoded in the committed inputs.

ceilings.relativity_note: Relative to the formal argumentation semantics of finite defeasible rule systems: the ceiling names ideal / sceptical-preferred acceptance (Dung-Mancarella-Toni; sceptical acceptance over the complete preferred-extension set) as the acceptance relation, with the grounded/well-founded extension (Dung; Van Gelder-Ross-Schlipf well-founded model) as the tractable-unique rung, grounded STRICTLY CONTAINED in ideal. Correctness claims are meaningful only against the committed formal semantics of the admitted rulebase, never against 'the law' as natural-language text.

Prove: (T1) Phi has a unique least fixpoint wf(G) computed in <= |N| rounds (termination + uniqueness, deterministic replay); (T2) soundness — every node labelled in possesses a finite well-founded derivation tree all of whose defeaters are labelled out; (T3) completeness — every node in the well-founded model is labelled in; (T4) defeater sensitivity — adding any admitted defeater d attacking node n either flips n to out/undefined or yields a certificate that d is itself out; (T5) UNKNOWN monotonicity — undefined never satisfies the acceptance predicate; (T6) ideal-rung theorems — the ideal extension ideal(G) is unique, deterministic, and decidable over finite G; grounded(G) is a subset of ideal(G); exhibit a finite even-cycle witness graph with grounded(G) strictly contained in ideal(G) (the recorded gap); the exhaustive-extension certificate checker accepts a certificate iff it enumerates exactly the preferred extensions of G. All statements are about total functions on finite structures, formalizable in Lean 4.

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum achievable plan-decomposition assurance under H1-H8 is: for a plan that is a DETERMINISTIC DERIVATION FROM FROZEN INPUTS (a pure function of the committed closure — pre-commitment of the plan artifact is one sufficient realization, not a necessity) into a finite, explicitly typed dataflow DAG with a declared goal-artifact set, ALL defects in the decidable defect class — cyclic dependency, produces/consumes artifact-type mismatch on any edge, goal artifact unreachable from admitted inputs, orphan stage feeding no goal, ambiguous execution order — are made structurally inadmissible at plan-derivation time (fail-closed, H3); the admitted plan has a unique deterministic total schedule (H5); the plan carries a certificate any third party re-derives from the committed inputs alone (H8); AND the decidable class extends to declared-finite-domain planning: VAL-class precondition/effect validation of a candidate plan against a committed finite-domain action model, and sound+complete plan SYNTHESIS over committed finite domains emitting existence certificates (a valid plan with its validation trace) or nonexistence certificates (an exhaustive refutation over the finite state space). No feasible system can additionally verify completeness of the plan relative to informal human intent, nor decide plan existence over unbounded action spaces.
ceilings.derivation: (1) Verification theory: completeness relative to intent is not computable — the intent is not encoded; only completeness relative to a committed formal goal specification is machine-checkable (same underdetermination as AX-01). (2) Complexity, corrected: general plan synthesis is PSPACE-complete over finite STRIPS domains and undecidable over infinite domains — but PSPACE-completeness is a cost fact, not an impossibility: over a COMMITTED FINITE domain, plan validation is linear-time decidable and plan existence/synthesis is decidable with checkable certificates, so the feasible decidable class strictly exceeds the five structural DAG checks; the ceiling includes finite-domain synthesis-with-certificates, with cost governed by AX-17 budgets. H5 requires the plan be a PURE FUNCTION of frozen inputs — 'committed before execution' is a sufficient discipline, not the requirement itself: a deterministic planner over a committed finite domain yields replayable synthesized plans that satisfy H5/H6 identically. Against a committed finite DAG, every structural property in the defect class is decidable in O(V+E) with linear-time-checkable certificates; therefore FULL exclusion of the decidable class, not statistical reduction, is feasible — elimination of the error class is the ceiling, guarding against instances is below it. (3) Determinism: among valid schedules, uniqueness is achievable at zero cost (topological sort with total lexicographic tie-break); any nondeterministic schedule strictly violates H5. Exceeding this ceiling requires deciding intent (not encoded) or verifying unbounded plan spaces (undecidable).

ceilings.relativity_note: Relative to a committed typed-DAG plan semantics (finite stages with declared produces/consumes artifact types and a declared goal-artifact set) extended by a committed finite-domain action model for validation/synthesis. All over Finset/List with decidable predicates — Lean 4 formalizable.

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum achievable contradiction/uncertainty/coverage/blind-spot handling under H1-H8 is certified totality over FOUR verdict classes: every query against the committed corpus and rulebase returns exactly one of {PASS with recomputable certificate; FAIL/CONTRADICTION with recomputable counter-certificate; PASS/FAIL-STABLE-OVER-UNKNOWNS — a KNOWN verdict derived over UNKNOWN inputs carrying a certified invariance (stability) certificate proving the verdict identical under ALL completions of the unknown inputs; typed UNKNOWN carrying a machine-readable reason drawn from a CLOSED, committed enumeration of unknowability causes} — where (a) contradiction detection is provably complete WITHIN a declared decidable class over the committed inputs, (b) the boundary of that class is itself a committed, certificate-carrying, machine-enforced artifact (not prose), (c) coverage is a positively-proven census (absence of a check is itself a detectable, blocking state — no silent gap), and (d) UNKNOWN propagates to every derived fact EXCEPT one carrying a certified invariance (stability) proof that its value is identical under all completions of the unknown input — the input itself remains UNKNOWN, the derived verdict is KNOWN-with-stability-certificate, and absence of such a certificate leaves the derived fact UNKNOWN, terminal, never defaulted to pass/equality (H2), with any flagged anomaly a blocking, non-servable state (H3). No feasible system can additionally certify the absence of unknown-unknowns outside its committed input set, or decide consistency of theories beyond its declared decidable class.
ceilings.derivation: (1) Computability: consistency of an unrestricted first-order theory is undecidable (and by Goedel II an expressive consistent system cannot prove its own consistency), so 'detects all contradictions' is impossible simpliciter; the supremum is completeness within a declared decidable class plus a checkable declaration of that class's boundary. (2) Information theory: blind spots over inputs never received are undetectable in principle; the ceiling for blind-spot handling is 'no SILENT blind spots over the committed universe': a positively-proven coverage census in which every element of the committed corpus is checked-with-certificate or explicitly enumerated as unchecked. (3) H8: a declared all-clear can never exceed what an independent recomputation over committed inputs establishes. (4) Stability carve-out, corrected from v1: UNCONDITIONAL propagation of UNKNOWN is strictly below the attainable maximum. Certified invariance discharge — three-valued Kleene evaluation, exhaustive case-split, exact stability computation — soundly derives a KNOWN verdict over UNKNOWN inputs whenever the verdict is invariant over ALL completions of the unknown (trivially A or True = True for unknown A; non-trivially a verdict stable over all completions of an unknown dimension). This is not guessing: the certificate quantifies over completions and is offline-recheckable (H2 intact), deterministic (H5), and fail-closed (no invariance certificate, UNKNOWN stands). Without this carve-out a derived verdict provably invariant to an unknown would be withheld — an information-destroying rule, and one that would block tournament verdicts on pairs whose outcome is invariant to the unknown axis. Where evidence about an external candidate supports only a KNOWN_UPPER_BOUND cap rather than a rank, the derived verdict class is the cap, never a rank (see freeze v2). The whole argument is model-independent for any H1-H8 system.

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. For any system satisfying H1-H8, the maximum attainable grounding of a served legal text t is: (i) ORIGIN AUTHENTICITY no stronger than what can be TRANSPORTED, CORROBORATED, or CHANNEL-ATTESTED — (a) transport: verification of the official publisher's cryptographic signature over the captured bytes, bounded by the publisher's PKI; (b) corroboration: agreement of a k-of-n quorum of independent, contemporaneous capture witnesses over the byte digest, whose assurance is a MONOTONE FUNCTION of the declared witness set's size and independence — a resource-parameterized bound with no absolute maximum; (c) attested-channel capture: a TLS-oracle protocol (DECO/TLSNotary-class) or TEE-attested fetcher binding the received bytes to the publisher's TLS channel identity at capture time, transporting origin assurance through the publisher's channel key where the content is unsigned, at the cost of the respective protocol or hardware-vendor trust anchor; anything below these is admissible only as typed UNKNOWN/provisional. NEGATIVE HALF (the only ABSOLUTE clause): no local computation over already-held bytes can create origin authenticity after the fact — a digest commits to WHAT was received, never to WHO published it. Plus (ii) DERIVATION BINDING — a deterministic, third-party re-executable extraction function E with byte-equality E(captured-bytes) = t, committed as a dual digest; plus (iii) CORPUS-SIZE INDEPENDENCE — Grounded(t) mentions only the committed capture record of t's own source (selection by exact committed identifier, never by search/glob/statistics), invariant under corpus extension, with membership verification O(log n) via Merkle inclusion — optimal among hash-based schemes with no setup assumptions (constant-size membership proofs exist under other assumption families, e.g. RSA accumulators and vector commitments, at the cost of those assumptions).
ceilings.derivation: The negative half is information-theoretic and model-independent: authenticity of bytes fetched from a network endpoint cannot be created after the fact by any local computation. The POSITIVE mechanisms number three, not two (v1 corrected): (a) signature transport — a key predating the capture, rooted in the publisher; (b) independent corroboration — k witnesses on disjoint trust/network paths committing the same digest at capture time, forgery requiring compromise of all k or the endpoint itself, with assurance monotone in the declared witness set (hence resource-parameterized, no absolute cap); (c) attested-channel capture — origin assurance transported through the publisher's TLS channel identity via an oracle protocol or attested fetcher, strictly stronger than a bare single-witness digest and independent of (a) and (b), introducing a protocol/hardware trust anchor of the same category as the genesis anchors AX-12 accepts. H1 forbids substituting a statistical model's authenticity judgment; H8 forbids trusting the producer's declared root. Part (ii): 'served text derives from primary bytes' is zero-trust checkable only for a pure deterministic derivation compared byte-for-byte — the ceiling is deterministic-replay equality. Part (iii): any grounding predicate consulting corpus-global state breaks replay under corpus growth and adds zero authenticity; O(log n) Merkle inclusion suffices and is optimal among hash-based, setup-free schemes.
ceilings.ceiling_kind: ABSOLUTE (negative half: no after-the-fact authenticity) / RESOURCE_BOUNDED (positive clauses: publisher PKI, witness-set parameterization, attested-channel trust anchors)
ceilings.relativity_note: The positive origin-assurance clauses are parameterized by declared resources: the publisher's signing practice, the declared witness set (witness networks are operational today — enrolling is a feasible act, not an unreachable resource), and the availability of an attested-channel stack. Only the negative half is model- and resource-independent.
ceilings.lean_obligation: With hash : Bytes -> Digest collision-resistant (axiom), E : Bytes -> ServedText total computable, sigOK : PublisherKey -> Bytes -> Sig -> Prop, chanOK : ChannelAnchor -> Bytes -> Attestation -> Prop, and a finite witness set W: define Grounded t c := (transport OR quorum(k) OR channel-attested) AND E c.bytes = t. Prove: (T-ceiling) any grounding predicate P satisfying H5 and H8 implies P t -> Grounded t (Grounded is the supremum of the three-mechanism family); (T-negative) no predicate computable from already-held bytes alone, without a transport, quorum, or channel witness, entails origin authenticity — formalized as: for any such P there exist two capture histories with identical held bytes and different true origins that P cannot separate; (T-monotone) quorum assurance is monotone in (k, independence structure of W) — the corroboration bound is a function of the declared witness set, not a constant; (T-attain) the admission predicate equals Grounded; (T-size-indep) for corpora C subset C', Grounded t c holds in C iff in C', and Merkle inclusion verification is O(log |C|).

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Relative to a declared decidable citation grammar G for the legal order and a fixed authority-chain semantics, the maximum attainable by any H1-H8 system is: SOUND AND COMPLETE PROOF-CARRYING RESOLUTION OVER L(G) — every string in L(G) occurring in served text is parsed by a total, coverage-gated recognizer and resolved to exactly one committed authority record carrying a verified receipt (signature chain valid to a pinned owner key, delegation valid at the receipt's genTime, revocation checked, bitemporal validity covering the citation's reference time), and every citation-like string outside L(G) is emitted as typed UNKNOWN-CITATION that never upgrades to a pass (H2). SEMANTIC SUPPORT, split honestly (v1 corrected): for propositions that are FORMAL OBJECTS of the system, support-verification is INSIDE the ceiling — derivation provenance makes it decidable: the conclusion's certified derivation uses rule R, whose admission record binds R to a pinpoint span S of authority A, so 'the cited authority is the recorded basis of the citing proposition' is a zero-LLM decidable predicate attained by AX-01 x AX-04 composition. What remains excluded for every feasible system is NL-vs-NL support — verification that a natural-language authority text semantically supports a natural-language proposition — and recognition of arbitrary natural-language reference intent outside G; claiming either without human adjudication is structurally dishonest under H1.
ceilings.derivation: Computability: the set of NL strings that function as citations has no decidable characterization; any total mechanical recognizer fixes a formal language, so the ceiling is stated relative to a declared decidable G. H1 closes the escape: a statistical model approximating NL intent is banned from the trusted path; its output is an untrusted CANDIDATE re-entering through the G-verifier. Within L(G), verification theory gives the maximum: binding to an authority record whose authenticity chain is checkable offline with zero producer trust (H8) — signature to pinned root, delegation window containment, revocation absence, bitemporal validity — the strongest offline-checkable statement about the citation's TARGET; authority-ness beyond the committed chain reduces to the AX-04 origin ceiling. The semantic-support impossibility is SCOPED (v1 overshoot corrected): it applies to NL-proposition-vs-NL-authority support, which requires an oracle for legal meaning; formal-proposition support reduces to derivation provenance over committed admission records — decidable, inside the ceiling. Consistency: the JWS layer proves internal consistency, not authenticity; authenticity enters only through the pinned-owner chain.
ceilings.ceiling_kind: MODEL_RELATIVE
ceilings.relativity_note: Relative to: (1) a declared decidable citation grammar G for the legal order; (2) a TUF-style delegation semantics with owner-key pinning; (3) a bitemporal validity semantics (valid-time x transaction-time with a genTime floor). Change any of the three and the ceiling statement changes with it. Witness instantiation (Greek FEK/ELI grammar and the B0 seats): appendix.
ceilings.lean_obligation: Fix G with decidable membership, receipts R with decidable chainValid and validAt predicates over committed bytes, resolve : {s // s in L G} -> Option R pure, out : String -> Result total. (3) Fail-closed totality (H2+H3): an erring gate predicate has produced UNKNOWN, which never upgrades to pass; the ceiling gate maps every non-proof path to a refusal that is itself a derivation (which conjunct, over which committed facts), durably recorded; 'never wrongly refuse' would require deciding properties of arbitrary future predicates (Rice), so refusal stays cheap, recorded, and creator-overridable only via an explicit reason-carrying logged override. (4) Equivocation bound (SUNDR), relabeled: with a single writer and no independent witnesses, fork consistency is the provable maximum; full split-view resistance requires an external cosigning quorum. That quorum is a DEPLOYMENT RESOURCE — witness networks with shared vetted configurations operate across ecosystems today, so the v1 phrase 'not within unilateral reach today' is retracted; by the corpus's own labeling standard (a resource that would strictly lift the cap, excluded only by declared scope) this clause is RESOURCE_BOUNDED. The process-not-substance clause follows from H1: judging legal-substantive correctness would put a model in the trusted path; the ceiling system makes the boundary of its own authority a committed, checkable artifact.

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Auditability terminates at the commitment boundary: nothing outside the committed closure (e.g., what the publisher's server really served at capture time) is auditable in principle — the strongest attainable is a signed/witnessed/channel-attested capture receipt committing the bytes at ingestion. COST clause (RESOURCE_BOUNDED): linear-cost recomputation is the operative verification cost only for a declared toolchain lacking an arithmetization of its pipeline; a transparent proof toolchain strictly lowers verifier cost with no assurance loss.
ceilings.derivation: Verification theory admits exactly two zero-trust offline verification modes: recompute-and-compare, and proof-checking. The v1 dismissal of mode (b) is corrected on two counts: (1) it rested on a false cryptographic premise — transparent (STARK-class) proof systems have NO trusted setup; their assumptions are collision-resistant hashing, the same family the ceilings already accept for SHA-256 commitments — so mode (b) adds no new trust CATEGORY, only a proof-system soundness reduction within the same family; (2) 'arithmetizing the pipeline is infeasible' is a toolchain/cost fact, which may not appear inside an ABSOLUTE label — it is carved into the RESOURCE_BOUNDED cost clause. H8's semantic content is zero producer trust; both modes satisfy it and are equally maximal in assurance, so 'recompute-and-compare is the ceiling' is restated as 'derivability-from-committed-bytes under stated assumptions is the ceiling, attained by either mode'. The boundary claim is information-theoretic and stands: two histories producing identical committed byte-closures are indistinguishable to any auditor; past states of external sources are not replayable, hence capture receipts (signed, witnessed, or channel-attested per AX-04) are the maximum for origin bytes. Completeness of the closure is capped by what was committed — an audit is exactly as strong as the closure is total.
ceilings.ceiling_kind: ABSOLUTE (assurance clause: audit knowledge bounded by the committed closure under stated hash assumptions) / RESOURCE_BOUNDED (cost clause)

Nothing exceeds output = f(committed closure); any residual dependence on an uncommitted quantity is nondeterminism by definition. ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. On the declared operating model (single node, POSIX filesystem, commodity SSD with honored write barriers), the maximum achievable is: (a) DURABILITY — a state transition is durable exactly when its data, metadata, and directory entry have reached stable media behind an explicit write barrier (fsync of file AND containing directory); acknowledged-but-unsynced data is unrecoverable in principle; single-device durability is bounded by media survival — nothing short of replication (outside the declared model, a resource not an impossibility) exceeds it. (b) CRASH CONSISTENCY — atomicity of accountable transitions: after a crash at ANY point, recovery yields a state equal to applying some prefix of the committed transition sequence, with every barrier-acknowledged transition included and no torn/partial artifact ever observable (H6 as a maximum). (c) BOUNDED RECOVERY — recovery work is Theta(uncommitted tail since last checkpoint), capped by checkpointing; no scheme recovers in less than the time to read what recovery must read. (d) FAIL-CLOSED READ-BACK — a transition counts committed only after recompute-and-compare of the persisted bytes (H3/H8).
ceilings.derivation: Storage physics: volatile memory does not survive power loss, so durability of information not yet behind a stable-media barrier is impossible — the fsync wait is the definition of the durable point on the declared platform. Atomicity: the storage stack provides only small atomic primitives; any larger unit is constructed by a commit protocol requiring at least one ordering barrier between data and commit record; the minimal shape 'intent, data barrier, atomic switch, directory barrier' is what every known correct protocol reduces to (the reduction claim is discharged as the AX-11 obligation, shared). Prefix semantics is the consistency ceiling: a crash lands between any two barriers, so the strongest single-node invariant is 'some committed prefix, monotone, nothing torn'; promising more violates physics, promising less violates H3/H6. Recovery lower bound is counting: recovery must read the journal tail it replays.

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Under the declared operating model (single node, fair scheduler, eventually-available storage, finite committed inputs, external calls that may fail forever), the maximum achievable liveness is CONDITIONAL BOUNDED TERMINATION: every admitted task reaches, within an explicit per-task budget B(task), exactly one of three terminal states — SUCCESS with certificate, typed FAIL, or typed UNKNOWN/REFUSED — with no livelock, no unbounded retry, and no silent hang; retries are idempotent so a re-attempt after partial failure has exactly-once observable effect on committed state; after a crash, work resumes from the last checkpoint with bounded re-execution. Unconditional liveness is UNACHIEVABLE by any system honoring H3 — blocking on persistent environment misbehavior is forced, and the ceiling converts every such block into a typed, bounded-time refusal rather than a hang.
ceilings.derivation: (1) Fail-closed vs progress trade-off: H3 requires blocking on error/violation/unknown; an adversarial environment can stall any H3-compliant system indefinitely, so progress is only ever conditional on declared environment assumptions; the maximum is making the condition explicit and the failure mode a bounded-time typed refusal (H2). Safety-preserving systems buy liveness only from environment assumptions. (2) Exactly-once effects: at-least-once retry plus at-most-once effect requires idempotence/deduplication state — exactly-once delivery without a dedup record is classically impossible — so idempotency-keyed retries against a durable journal are the ceiling mechanism. (3) Termination cannot be inferred (halting), so the maximum feasible guarantee is termination BY CONSTRUCTION — every trusted loop carries a well-founded variant, making non-termination structurally impossible rather than tested-for. Bounded recovery follows from AX-15's checkpoint bound.

(2) Conditional progress: under Fair E and Avail E, an admitted task terminates in Success. (3) Retry idempotence: committedEffects (exec (exec s)) = committedEffects (exec s), from the journal-key check. (4) No silent degradation: markExecuted is only reachable from a stage-success derivation — the failed-marked-executed defect class is unrepresentable.

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. For latency over a frozen workload distribution, the maximum assurance any H1-H8 system can provide is: (a) an EXACT, offline-verifiable deterministic cost certificate — for every workload item x, a cost value C(f,x) in abstract units (operations executed, bytes hashed, bytes consed, stage invocations) that any third party recomputes to bit-equality, so every quantile of the cost distribution over the frozen workload is a theorem, not a sample; plus (b) a fail-closed cost-budget gate blocking any run whose certified cost exceeds a committed budget; plus (c) a wall-clock claim whose CEILING is K-OF-N EXTERNAL-TIME-AUTHORITY BRACKETING (v1 corrected — producer attestation is NOT the maximum): an offline-verifiable wall-clock BRACKET on a run, obtained by binding committed run events to timestamps from k of n independent external time authorities — Roughtime-class malfeasance-provable timestamps, qualified (eIDAS-class) timestamp authorities, timestamped witness cosignatures — verified against pinned third-party keys with ZERO PRODUCER TRUST, the residue being trust in the external time quorum; the weaker form 'certified cost x attested machine rate r' (producer-signed rate) remains admissible as a typed lower rung. No system can make wall-clock seconds offline-verifiable with zero trust in ANY party; with zero PRODUCER trust, external-authority bracketing is the supremum.
ceilings.derivation: (1) No-go, restated precisely: wall-clock duration is not a pure function of committed inputs — a replaying verifier obtains a different number — so wall-clock is never verifiable by recomputation alone. The v1 conclusion that producer attestation is therefore the ceiling was too weak: interval BRACKETING by independent external time authorities yields offline-verifiable upper (and lower) bounds on a run's wall-clock extent against pinned third-party keys — zero producer trust, with trust relocated to an external quorum whose malfeasance is provable (Roughtime-class) or legally accountable (qualified timestamps). Hence the wall-clock ceiling is k-of-n external-time-authority bracketing; producer-signed machine rate is a strictly weaker rung. (2) Exactness of the fully-zero-third-party-trust part: because H5 makes the derivation deterministic, the multiset {C(f,x)} over the frozen workload is a computable function of the committed workload — mean, p50, p99, max are exactly computable and re-derivable; sampling error is eliminated entirely. (3) H3 permits the strongest enforcement compatible with the no-go: a fail-closed blocking budget gate on certified cost. The abstract-cost certificate remains the only component requiring zero trust in ANY third party; the bracketing clause is resource-parameterized by the declared time-authority set.

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Resource-normalized throughput of any H1-H8 system on p workers is bounded by T_p >= max(W/p, S, ceil(n/b) * c_batch): W = total verification/generation work, S = span of the input dependency DAG, and ceil(n/b) * c_batch = the BATCHED AMORTIZED serialization floor for appending n accountable transitions through the single logical serialization point (H4/H6) in batches of b — batched Merkle appends amortize to O(1) hashing per item with O(log n) proof material per append, so the floor is per-BATCH serialization, not per-transition ('irreducibly serial per transition' is retracted). Verification work W has an operative floor under the declared toolchain: a zero-producer-trust verifier in recompute mode must read and hash every committed byte at least once, so throughput is capped by min(I/O bandwidth, hash bandwidth) per admitted byte; on unchanged inputs, content-addressed memoization reduces work to the delta plus one digest comparison per cached unit. Sublinear verification via succinct TRANSPARENT proof systems (no trusted setup; hash-family assumptions) is not cryptographically excluded — its absence here is a declared-toolchain/arithmetization cost fact, which is exactly what the RESOURCE_BOUNDED kind records. The ceiling is attained by deterministic parallel-map with ordered serial fold; all bounds derived from committed corpus configuration, never constants.
ceilings.derivation: (1) Serialization floor, corrected: H4 plus H6 force a total order on admissions — one logical serialization point (physical single writer, or machine-checked nonforking replicated order); commit throughput is bounded by that point's sequential rate, and the optimum is batched commitment: group b transitions per batch, one serialized append per batch, per-item cost one hash amortized, O(log n) proof material — hence the floor ceil(n/b) * c_batch, which the attainment schedule itself uses. (2) Work/span law (Brent): any p-worker schedule has makespan >= max(W/p, S) — implementation-independent. (3) Verification floor, restated honestly: under zero producer trust in RECOMPUTE mode, trusting k bytes requires reading k bytes (Omega(k) I/O and hashing). The v1 exclusion of succinct proofs by 'trusted setup' was false — STARK-class systems are transparent; the honest exclusion ground is toolchain/arithmetization cost only, so the linear floor is OPERATIVE (toolchain-relative), not absolute — consistent with the AX-06/AX-13 v2 split. (4) Determinism costs nothing asymptotically: parallel-map with deterministic ordered reduction achieves the same T_p bound with byte-identical output — any design paying throughput for determinism is below ceiling.
ceilings.ceiling_kind: RESOURCE_BOUNDED
ceilings.relativity_note: The linear verification floor and the batch constant c_batch are relative to the declared toolchain and storage/hash bandwidth; the work/span law and the existence of a serialization floor are model-independent.
ceilings.lean_obligation: Theorem (schedule optimality with batched accountable commit): for a dependency DAG with work W and span S, and a total-ordered commit relation with per-batch cost c_batch and batch size b, every conforming p-worker schedule satisfies T_p >= max (W/p) (max S (ceil(n/b) * c_batch)), and the ordered-parallel-map/serial-fold schedule achieves T_p <= W/p + S + ceil(n/b) * c_batch with output extensionally equal to the sequential schedule. Amortization lemma: total hashing over n batched appends is O(n) with O(log n) proof material per append. Verification floor lemma (recompute mode): a sound zero-producer-trust recomputing verifier over committed bytes b reads at least |b| positions (indistinguishability of strings differing at an unread index). Incremental floor: unchanged cached unit re-verifies in exactly one digest comparison.

ceilings.ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. The maximum inspectable causal account any H1-H8 system can give for a trusted decision is the decision's own replayable derivation: a trace, recomputable to bit-equality by third parties from committed inputs (H5/H8), in which every trusted effect appears exactly once with its cause chain back to committed inputs. Completeness of the account equals completeness of effect mediation (H4 capability closure), and — THE RELATIVITY STATED HERE, IN THE STATEMENT — it is attainable at TWO RUNGS: (RUNG 1, structural, available without verified-compilation resources) a construction-level local invariant of the single mediation seat making effect-execution and trace-emission the same event inside the same all-or-nothing transition (H6), so an untraced trusted act is structurally impossible relative to the declared effect semantics, with absence of out-of-model effects enforced by the OS capability model, not proven of arbitrary code; (RUNG 2, strictly stronger, gated on AX-21 verified-compilation/verification resources) machine-checked whole-perimeter verification of the mediator and runtime, proving of the code itself that no effect path bypasses the mediation seat — Rice bars DECIDING arbitrary code, not VERIFYING constrained code that carries proofs. Two hard limits bound both rungs from above: (a) no explanation can carry more causal information than the derivation itself — every sound account is a function of the replay trace; (b) a causal account of WHY an untrusted candidate was proposed (statistical-producer internals, H1) is out of trusted scope — the admission/refusal derivation is the entire trusted causal story.
ceilings.derivation: (1) Information-theoretic supremum: under H5 a trusted decision is a pure finite computation from committed inputs; the full derivation determines the decision and every true causal statement about it; any account not derivable from the trace asserts causation the computation does not contain (barred by H2). The ceiling is reached when the account IS the derivation, verified by recompute (H8). (2) Structural completeness, honestly two-runged (v1 corrected — the v1 text presented the local-invariant form as the maximum simpliciter while its own parenthetical conceded the stronger route): global no-bypass is undecidable for ARBITRARY code (Rice), but that does not cap proof-carrying constrained code — whole-perimeter verification is a feasible mechanism class gated on declared verification resources, so rung 1 is the maximum only relative to declining those resources, and the ceiling names both rungs. (3) H1 boundary: statistical-producer internals admit no faithful causal account with today's tools, and H1 makes this irrelevant — the candidate is data; the admission derivation over it is the complete trusted causal account. (4) Determinism of the account: the trace is a pure function of committed inputs, so independent verifiers derive identical accounts — explanation itself is replayable.

No system can certify refutation-completeness over the open class of all possible defects OUTSIDE its committed specs and committed finite classes — completeness claims are always relative to the committed spec/class registry.
ceilings.derivation: Computability, applied honestly: Rice's theorem makes non-trivial semantic properties of arbitrary code undecidable — no total procedure DECIDES 'no superior counter-design exists' or 'no undetected defect exists'. But proof-CHECKING is decidable: a candidate arriving with a machine-checked proof is admitted by a total decidable check, and the proof refutes an infinite defect class relative to its spec — so the v1 ceiling (finite-class kill as the maximum) was strictly below the attainable maximum on any verified perimeter. Verification theory (Popper asymmetry): universal correctness claims are refutable, never verifiable — EXCEPT relative to a committed formal spec, where a correctness proof is exactly a refutation-completeness certificate for the spec'd class; outside specs, the strongest coherent artifact is a corroboration certificate relative to a committed enumerable falsifier class (hashed, else the certificate is itself unfalsifiable). Consistency: self-graded falsifiers without an externally recomputable kill matrix trust a declared root (H8 violation); continuing past a surviving mutant is silent degradation (H3 violation). The v1 closing phrase 'nothing feasible today exceeds it' is deleted — resource phrasing may not appear inside an ABSOLUTE label; the ceiling is stated as the two-regime structure itself.

No system transports a property to the executable with a smaller trust residue than this TCB, and no property is transported beyond what the weakest link carries. ceilings.derivation: Verification theory: every proof chain bottoms out in an unverified checker plus hardware — the TCB is irreducible, only minimizable (a self-verifying checker is circular; Goedel II blocks self-certified consistency). Thompson's trusting-trust result: compiler trust cannot be discharged by source inspection alone; the mitigations are a verified compiler, diverse double-compilation, or independent re-execution of artifact-level claims. For a toolchain WITH a verified compiler substrate available (CakeML/Brack-class, which exists and is obtainable offline today), the compiler link becomes link-type (a) and the TCB strictly shrinks; for a declared toolchain WITHOUT one, link-type (b) is the optimum for the compiler link. Information-theoretic: a property claim about the executable carries at most the information transported through the chain; any claim exceeding the conjunction of link guarantees is unverifiable assertion (H8). Therefore ceiling = machine-checked links where a checker exists + recompute-and-compare links elsewhere + committed enumerated TCB — RESOURCE_BOUNDED because the verified substrate strictly shrinks the TCB and its exclusion is only a declared commitment.
